function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

"""Field projections shared by employee-facing account-directory endpoints."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any


PUBLIC_ACCOUNT_FIELDS = (
    "employee_id",
    "username",
    "department",
    "host_group",
    "status",
)


def public_account(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the employee-directory fields approved for general visibility."""

    return {field: record[field] for field in PUBLIC_ACCOUNT_FIELDS if field in record}

# Server-account directory

This standard-library service backs an employee self-service portal. Complete the
three unfinished query functions in `account_service.py` using the public account
projection and contracts in `docs/server_accounts.md`.

Run the repository checks with:

```bash
make test
```

The service reads `fixtures/accounts.json` by default. Tests and deployments may
select another JSON fixture through `ACCOUNT_DATA`.

# Server-account query development guide

The account directory is consumed by the employee self-service portal. Department
and host-group arguments match the stored values exactly and case-sensitively.

## Query contract

- `list_accounts_by_department(department)` returns matching public account records
  sorted by `username`, then `employee_id`. It returns `[]` when nothing matches.
- `list_accounts_by_host_group(host_group)` returns matching public account records
  in the same order and returns `[]` when nothing matches.
- `count_accounts_by_department(department)` returns an integer and returns `0` for
  an unknown department.

Use `account_fields.public_account()` for account records returned to the general
employee directory. `get_directory_account()` demonstrates that projection.

"""Public-record query examples for the server-account directory."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from typing import Any

from account_fields import public_account


def copy_sorted_public_records(
    records: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Project records and place them in the directory's stable order."""

    projected = [public_account(record) for record in records]
    return sorted(
        projected,
        key=lambda record: (record["username"], record["employee_id"]),
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from account_service import (
    count_accounts_by_department,
    get_directory_account,
    list_accounts_by_department,
    list_accounts_by_host_group,
)


def employee_ids(records):
    return [record["employee_id"] for record in records]


class AccountServiceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_existing_directory_lookup_uses_public_shape(self):
        account = get_directory_account("E001")
        self.assertEqual(account["username"], "alice")
        self.assertNotIn("initial_password", account)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", account)
        self.assertNotIn("privilege_rules", account)

    def test_lists_department_in_documented_order(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            employee_ids(list_accounts_by_department("Engineering")),
            ["E003", "E004"],
        )
        self.assertEqual(list_accounts_by_department("Missing"), [])

    def test_lists_host_group_in_documented_order(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            employee_ids(list_accounts_by_host_group("prod-web")),
            ["E002", "E003"],
        )
        self.assertEqual(list_accounts_by_host_group("missing"), [])

    def test_counts_departments(self):
        self.assertEqual(count_accounts_by_department("Finance"), 2)
        self.assertEqual(count_accounts_by_department("Engineering"), 2)
        self.assertEqual(count_accounts_by_department("Support"), 2)
        self.assertEqual(count_accounts_by_department("Missing"), 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
